rationale: Continuing the authorized source work on the deferred transport surface: reading the pipelined path end to end, both its transport side and its protocol-side consumer, so the surface is bounded further and the ordering contract it depends on is recorded. feedback.answered: The pipelined AppendEntries path is now sourced. On the transport side, netPipeline sends the request first and then hands the future to inprogressCh, while a single decodeResponses goroutine takes futures from that channel in order, decodes one response per future on the same connection and publishes completed futures on doneCh (net_transport.go 817-905); the channel is sized maxInFlight-2 so at most maxInFlight requests are outstanding, and Close releases the connection and closes shutdownCh. On the protocol side, pipelineSend advances its local next-index optimistically by the number of entries sent as soon as the request is accepted by the pipeline (replication.go 512-530), and pipelineDecode consumes the pipeline consumer channel in order: a response with a newer term stops the leader's replication via handleStaleTerm, the first non-success response aborts the whole pipeline by returning (replication.go 534-565), and only successful responses call updateLastAppended, which is what records the peer's match index and moves the shared nextIndex. So request/response correlation for the pipeline is FIFO-by-construction and requires the transport to deliver responses in send order on one connection; the library's recovery from any pipeline error is to abandon pipelining and fall back to the synchronous path rather than to resynchronise inside the pipeline.
remaining: The connection pool lifecycle is still unread: getConn/getPooledConn/returnConn, reconnect and dead-connection handling, and what a pooled connection does when an RPC body fails mid-stream.

The listen/dispatch path is still unread: the RPC type dispatch table, how a message is decided to be a heartbeat and routed to the fast-path callback, per-message-type queueing into consumeCh, and behaviour under back-pressure.

TCPTransport's TLS and configuration wiring and InmemTransport's in-process delivery and ordering semantics are still unread; inmem_transport.go is the transport the captured tests exercise, so any ordering assumption there matters to how the repo's own evidence is produced.

The pipeline's optimistic next-index advance is read but not evaluated: whether abandoning the pipeline after a partially sent batch can leave the shared nextIndex above a point the peer has not acknowledged is a question for a future check, not a finding here.

Previously recorded open items are unchanged: installSnapshot watermark reachability from a legal leader history, the compacted-leader variant of the truncation-failure case, and execution corroboration of the two reading-based consequences.
